name: pterm-cell-addressable-textprinter-layouts
instr:
pterm cannot provide stable, cell-addressable terminal text layouts without losing semantic provenance. Implement immutable `TextLayout` rendering for selection, hit-testing, clipping, and composition while preserving Sprint-family bytes across ANSI styling, Unicode width, wrapping, alignment, and decoration.

From `github.com/pterm/pterm`, `BasicTextPrinter`, `Color`, `Style`, `RGB`, `RGBStyle`, `CenterPrinter`, `ParagraphPrinter`, `HeaderPrinter`, `SectionPrinter`, `BoxPrinter`, and `PrefixPrinter` must support `LayoutText` through `LayoutTextPrinter` without expanding `TextPrinter` for external implementations. Derive `Rendered`, `Lines`, terminal dimensions, and `Regions` from one rendering. Regions must distinguish displayed content from styling and generated margins, breaks, indentation, padding, fill, borders, titles, badges, prefixes, and line boundaries. Keep their hierarchy deterministic, contained, and noncrossing, with zero-width regions for empty content and generated breaks.

`PositionAtByte`, `ByteAtPosition`, `RuneOffsetAtByte`, and `ByteAtRuneOffset` must consistently map byte, rune, line, and cell coordinates without splitting ANSI controls or glyphs. Handle combining and zero-width runes, newlines, double-cell Unicode, and tabs at eight-cell stops. `RegionAt` returns the most specific semantic owner. Invalid positions, control-sequence interiors, partial glyphs, and positions in empty layouts return `ErrInvalidTextPosition` without affecting later results.
